001package io.github.ai4ci.functions;
002
003import java.io.Serializable;
004import java.util.Arrays;
005
006import org.immutables.value.Value;
007
008import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnore;
009import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
010import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeName;
011import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
012import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
013
014import io.github.ai4ci.functions.Coordinates.DuplicateResolution;
015
016/**
017 * An empirical kernel function.
018 *
019 * <p>
020 * This interface describes a kernel function defined by a set of discrete
021 * points. It includes methods to compute the minimum and maximum x values, and
022 * to construct an interpolator for the points. The interpolator is used to
023 * compute the raw value of the kernel at any given x.
024 *
025 * @author Rob Challen
026 */
027@Value.Immutable
028@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableEmpiricalKernel.class)
029@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableEmpiricalKernel.class)
030@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
031@JsonTypeName("empirical")
032public interface EmpiricalKernel extends Serializable, KernelFunction {
033
034        /**
035         * Constructs an interpolator for the kernel function based on the x and y
036         * values.
037         *
038         * <p>
039         * This method creates a {@link Coordinates} object from the x and y values,
040         * and then constructs a cubic spline interpolator using the
041         * {@link SplineInterpolator}. The interpolator can be used to compute the
042         * raw value of the kernel at any given x.
043         *
044         * <p>
045         * Note: The choice of cubic spline interpolation is a design decision; other
046         * interpolation methods could be used depending on the desired properties of
047         * the kernel function.
048         *
049         * @return an interpolator for the kernel function based on the x and y
050         *         values.
051         */
052        @JsonIgnore @Value.Derived
053        default Interpolator getInterpolator() {
054
055                Coordinates tmp = ImmutableCoordinates.builder()
056                        .setX(
057                                Arrays.stream(this.getT())
058                                        .asDoubleStream()
059                                        .toArray()
060                        )
061                        .setY(this.getY())
062                        .setXMin(this.getMinimum())
063                        .setXMax(this.getMaximum())
064                        .setXLink(LinkFunction.NONE)
065                        .setYLink(this.getLink())
066                        .setIncreasing(false)
067                        .setResolveDuplicates(DuplicateResolution.MEAN)
068                        .build();
069
070//              if (getX().length < 20) {
071
072                return SplineInterpolator.createCubicSpline(tmp.getHx(), tmp.getHy());
073
074//              } else {
075//                      return LoessInterpolator.createLoessInterpolator(tmp.getHx(), tmp.getHy());
076//              }
077        }
078
079        /**
080         * The link function applied to the y values.
081         *
082         * <p>
083         * This function is used to transform the y values before interpolation. The
084         * default is {@link LinkFunction#NONE}, which means no transformation is
085         * applied. Other link functions can be used to model different types of
086         * relationships between x and y, such as logarithmic or logistic links.
087         *
088         * @return the link function applied to the y values, defaulting to NONE.
089         */
090        @Value.Default
091        default LinkFunction getLink() { return LinkFunction.NONE; }
092
093        /**
094         * Computes the maximum x value of the kernel function.
095         *
096         * <p>
097         * This method computes the maximum by streaming the x values and finding the
098         * maximum. It returns 0 if the array is empty, but in practice the array
099         * should contain valid x values for a meaningful kernel function.
100         *
101         * @return the maximum x value of the kernel function, or 0 if the array is
102         *         empty.
103         */
104        @Override @Value.Default
105        default int getMaximum() {
106                return Arrays.stream(this.getT())
107                        .max()
108                        .orElse(0);
109        }
110
111        /**
112         * Computes the minimum x value of the kernel function.
113         *
114         * <p>
115         * This method computes the minimum by streaming the x values and finding the
116         * minimum. It returns 0 if the array is empty, but in practice the array
117         * should contain valid x values for a meaningful kernel function.
118         *
119         * @return the minimum x value of the kernel function, or 0 if the array is
120         *         empty.
121         */
122        @Override @Value.Default
123        default int getMinimum() {
124                return Arrays.stream(this.getT())
125                        .min()
126                        .orElse(0);
127        }
128
129        /**
130         * The x values of the kernel function.
131         *
132         * <p>
133         * These values are used to construct the interpolator and to compute the
134         * minimum and maximum x values. They should be provided in ascending order
135         * for consistency, but the implementation will handle unsorted input.
136         *
137         * @return an array of integers representing the x values of the kernel
138         *         function.
139         */
140        int[] getT();
141
142        /**
143         * The y values of the kernel function.
144         *
145         * <p>
146         * These values are used to construct the interpolator. They should
147         * correspond to the x values in {@link #getT()} and be of the same length.
148         *
149         * @return an array of doubles representing the y values of the kernel
150         *         function.
151         *
152         */
153        double[] getY();
154
155        /**
156         * Computes the raw value of the kernel function at a given x.
157         *
158         * <p>
159         * This method uses the interpolator to compute the value at x, and then
160         * applies the inverse of the link function to transform it back to the
161         * original scale. The result is the raw value of the kernel function at x.
162         *
163         * @param x the input value for which to compute the kernel function
164         * @return the raw value of the kernel function at x
165         */
166        @Override
167        default double rawValue(int x) {
168                return this.getLink()
169                        .invFn(
170                                this.getInterpolator()
171                                        .interpolate(x)
172                        );
173        }
174
175}
